name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-8
summary: A soothing anti-redness cosmetic peptide (Neutrazen) with essentially no standalone human data.
lead: Palmitoyl tripeptide-8, marketed as Neutrazen, is a synthetic lipopeptide used in cosmetics for sensitive or redness-prone skin. It is promoted as calming irritation-related redness and discomfort.

name: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12
summary: An elastin-fragment cosmetic peptide (Biopeptide EL) with lab-level evidence and no clinical trials found.
lead: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12, sold as Biopeptide EL, is a synthetic fatty-acid-linked peptide derived from a repeating elastin sequence and used in anti-ageing creams. It is marketed as supporting skin elasticity.

name: Palmitoyl oligopeptide
summary: A generic palmitoylated peptide label in anti-ageing creams, with no clinical trial of its own.
lead: Palmitoyl oligopeptide is a generic cosmetic-ingredient name for short peptides linked to palmitic acid, used in anti-ageing creams as collagen-promoting "signal" ingredients. Patent literature lists fatty-acid-grafted peptides, specifically C16 palmitoyl oligopeptides, among agents said to promote collagen synthesis .

name: Manganese tripeptide-1
summary: A manganese-bound GHK-style peptide in serums for sun damage and dark spots, with one small study behind it.
lead: Manganese tripeptide-1 is a cosmetic ingredient consisting of a manganese complex of a tripeptide, described as the manganese analogue of the copper-binding peptide GHK. It is used in facial serums marketed for photodamaged skin, including uneven pigmentation.

name: Tripeptide-3
summary: A cosmetic peptide marketed for oil control, with one small 2024 delivery study as its published evidence.
lead: Tripeptide-3 is an INCI name for a short synthetic peptide used in cosmetics, including products aimed at reducing facial oiliness. Little is published about it under this name.

name: Tripeptide-10 citrulline
summary: A decorin-mimicking peptide meant to tidy collagen fibres, backed by in vitro data and one 24-person study.
lead: Tripeptide-10 citrulline (marketed as Decorinyl) is a synthetic peptide designed to mimic the collagen-binding behavior of decorin, a proteoglycan that regulates collagen fibre assembly. It is used in anti-aging cosmetics.

name: Acetyl hexapeptide-3
summary: The older name for Argireline, the topical 'Botox-alternative' peptide with modest, inconsistent evidence.
lead: Acetyl hexapeptide-3 is the earlier name for the cosmetic peptide now listed under the INCI name acetyl hexapeptide-8 and sold as Argireline. It is a six-amino-acid fragment (Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-NH2) of SNAP-25, a protein involved in neurotransmitter release . Wikipedia notes that the "-3" name is considered incorrect for this peptide .

name: Acetyl tetrapeptide-15
summary: A sensitive-skin soothing peptide with supplier data only; no independent studies found.
lead: Acetyl tetrapeptide-15, sold by its supplier under the trade name Skinasensyl, is a synthetic peptide used in cosmetics aimed at sensitive or reactive skin. A 2021 review describes it as derived from endomorphin-2, a mu-opioid receptor agonist, and proposes that it raises the excitability threshold of skin sensory nerves in an endorphin-like way .

name: Acetyl tetrapeptide-2
summary: A thymopoietin-mimic cosmetic peptide with cell-culture data and one combination-lotion hair study.
lead: Acetyl tetrapeptide-2 is a synthetic four-amino-acid peptide (acetyl-Lys-Asp-Val-Tyr) used in anti-aging and skin-firming cosmetics, sold by suppliers under names such as Thymulen 4 . It is described as mimicking thymopoietin, a thymus hormone, and is claimed to counter the age-related decline of thymic factors and to support skin immune defences and epidermal regeneration .

name: Acetyl dipeptide-1 cetyl ester
summary: A soothing peptide for sensitive skin with supplier data and one head-to-head trial showing no significant stinging benefit.
lead: Acetyl dipeptide-1 cetyl ester, marketed as Calmosensine (also written Neurosensine), is a synthetic peptide derivative used in soothing skincare for sensitive skin. A 2021 review describes it as derived from the dipeptide Tyr-Arg and proposes that it increases expression of the POMC gene, raising levels of MSH, ACTH and beta-endorphin, which in turn is thought to lower release of CGRP and so reduce stinging indirectly .

name: Pentapeptide-18
summary: An enkephalin-mimic peptide sold for expression lines; the human evidence is a retinol combination cream.
lead: Pentapeptide-18 (Tyr-D-Ala-Gly-Phe-Leu), sold by supplier Lipotec as Leuphasyl, is a cosmetic peptide marketed to soften expression lines. Papers describe it as an enkephalin mimic that is proposed to bind enkephalin receptors on nerve endings, close calcium channels and reduce acetylcholine release, a mechanism sometimes called 'Botox-like' .

name: Pentapeptide-3
summary: An ambiguous peptide name: historically KTTKS (Matrixyl), also tied to Vialox; little verified evidence.
lead: Pentapeptide-3 is a cosmetic peptide name that is ambiguous in the literature. Before 2006, the INCI name palmitoyl pentapeptide-3 referred to the Lys-Thr-Thr-Lys-Ser (KTTKS) peptide sold as Matrixyl, since renamed palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 . the available alias for this entry, Vialox, is separately marketed as a muscle-relaxing 'Botox-like' ingredient, and no loaded source describes it.

name: Oligopeptide-68
summary: A cosmetic peptide marketed as a tyrosinase inhibitor for brightening; human data are limited to small melasma studies of multi-ingredient products.
lead: Oligopeptide-68 is a synthetic cosmetic peptide that is marketed as a skin-brightening ingredient. In the dermatology literature it is described as a TGF-beta1 biomimetic oligopeptide that inhibits tyrosinase, the enzyme that drives melanin production .

name: Tetrapeptide-21
summary: A four-amino-acid (GEKG) matrix-supporting cosmetic peptide; research so far is on skin delivery and cell-culture effects, not human trials.
lead: Tetrapeptide-21 is a cosmetic peptide with the sequence GEKG that is used in anti-aging skincare. Published papers describe it as demonstrating anti-aging efficacy and stimulating collagen .

name: Acetyl tetrapeptide-3
summary: A hair-anchoring cosmetic peptide (found in Capixyl) tested only inside a multi-herbal combination against 3% minoxidil in one small trial.
lead: Acetyl tetrapeptide-3 is a cosmetic peptide used in topical hair products for thinning hair, commonly as part of the ingredient blend Capixyl, which also appears with biochanin A and ginseng extracts .

name: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-3
summary: A cosmetic signal peptide that shows up in serum ingredient lists, with no published human trials behind it.
lead: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-3 is a cosmetic ingredient classed among the signal peptides, short amino-acid chains attached to a fatty (palmitoyl) group and added to skin-care products. It appears by name in the ingredient lists of published patent compositions for topical products, where it is combined with plant extracts and other actives .

name: Deoxyarbutin
summary: A synthetic arbutin derivative that blocks tyrosinase in lab and animal work; human trial data are thin.
lead: Deoxyarbutin (dA) is a synthetic derivative of arbutin that inhibits tyrosinase, the enzyme that drives melanin production, and has been developed as a topical skin-lightening agent for hyperpigmentation such as age spots and melasma .

name: Aloesin
summary: An Aloe-derived tyrosinase inhibitor with lab-level evidence for lightening and no published trials found.
lead: Aloesin is a chromone glucoside isolated from the Aloe plant that has been studied as a topical skin-lightening agent because it inhibits tyrosinase, the key enzyme of melanin synthesis . It is also among the best-studied active constituents of Aloe vera alongside aloe-emodin, aloin, emodin and acemannan .

name: Ellagic acid
summary: A fruit-and-nut polyphenol sold as an antioxidant and brightener; no skin trials found.
lead: Ellagic acid is a naturally occurring polyphenol, the dilactone of hexahydroxydiphenic acid, found in foods such as pomegranates, raspberries, strawberries, walnuts and grapes, where it is released from ellagitannins . It is marketed as an antioxidant and, in some skin-care products, as a brightening ingredient.

name: 4-n-Butylresorcinol
summary: A tyrosinase inhibitor used in melasma and dark-spot serums, with several small randomized trials reporting improvement.
lead: 4-n-Butylresorcinol (also called butylresorcinol or rucinol) is a synthetic resorcinol derivative used in topical serums and creams aimed at hyperpigmentation such as melasma and age spots. It acts as a tyrosinase inhibitor .

name: Rhododendrol
summary: A cosmetic lightening agent withdrawn in 2013 after users developed patchy depigmentation (leukoderma).
lead: Rhododendrol (RD, related to raspberry ketone) is a phenolic compound that occurs naturally in Rhododendron and other plants and was developed as a melanin-synthesis inhibitor for skin-lightening cosmetics . It was used as a skin-whitening agent until July 2013, when reports emerged that users had developed patchy depigmentation (leukoderma), after which the products were withdrawn .

name: Monobenzone
summary: A prescription depigmenting cream for extensive vitiligo whose skin-whitening effect is permanent, which is why forums discuss it as a one-way option.
lead: Monobenzone, also called monobenzyl ether of hydroquinone (MBEH) or 4-(benzyloxy)phenol, is a topical depigmenting agent. In the United States it is a prescription-only drug used to permanently remove remaining skin pigment in people with extensive vitiligo, so that the unaffected skin matches the depigmented patches . Unlike milder skin-lightening ingredients, its effect is described in the literature as irreversible, because it leads to the loss of melanocytes, the pigment-producing cells .
claims: Monobenzone permanently lightens normal skin to a pale tone
It is a stronger version of hydroquinone and kojic acid
The effect can be undone if the user changes their mind
Monobenzone is a safe route to evenly lighter skin for people without vitiligo

name: Oxyresveratrol
summary: A mulberry-derived stilbene that strongly blocks tyrosinase in the lab, with no human skin trials behind the brightening claims.
lead: Oxyresveratrol (2,3',4,5'-tetrahydroxystilbene) is a plant-derived stilbenoid found in species of Morus (mulberry) and Artocarpus, among others . It is studied mainly for its strong inhibition of tyrosinase, the enzyme that carries out rate-limiting steps of melanin synthesis, and is therefore discussed as a potential skin-lightening ingredient .

name: Resveratrol topical
summary: An antioxidant stilbene sold in anti-aging serums, with one small recent trial and mostly delivery-formulation research behind it.
lead: Resveratrol (3,5,4'-trihydroxy-trans-stilbene) is a plant polyphenol found in grape skins, berries and peanuts, and in knotweed root used for supplements . Applied to the skin, it appears in anti-aging and brightening cosmetics, where it is marketed as an antioxidant .

name: Licochalcone A
summary: A licorice-root chalcone used in soothing skincare, with lab hints of tyrosinase inhibition and only combination-product acne trials in humans.
lead: Licochalcone A is a chalcone-type phenol isolated from the roots of licorice species (Glycyrrhiza inflata and G. glabra) . In skincare it appears in products for sensitive, red or acne-prone skin and is also discussed for its possible effect on pigment production .

name: Chitosan
summary: A shellfish-derived polysaccharide used as a carrier in cosmetics and sold as a fat binder, with no trial showing a skin-pigment or appearance effect.
lead: Chitosan is a linear polysaccharide made by partially deacetylating chitin, which is found mainly in the shells of shrimp and crabs and in some fungi and insects . It dissolves in dilute acid and is widely used in medicine, agriculture and industry, with cosmetic uses and weight-loss supplements being the applications most relevant to appearance .

name: Diacetyl boldine
summary: A boldo-derived tyrosinase-stabilizing brightener found in serums, with small combination-formula studies and no stand-alone trials.
lead: Diacetyl boldine (DAB) is a cosmetic skin-brightening ingredient derived from boldine, an aporphine alkaloid found in the bark of the boldo tree (Peumus boldus) . It is used in serums and creams aimed at hyperpigmentation, dark spots and melasma, usually as one component of a multi-ingredient formula.

name: Mulberry extract
summary: A botanical 'brightener' whose published research is about blood sugar and antioxidants, not skin tone.
lead: Mulberry extract is a plant extract from trees of the genus Morus, marketed in skincare as a botanical brightener, with mulberroside F named as its skin-lightening constituent. The fruit and leaves are also sold as dietary supplements .

name: Rice bran extract
summary: A K-beauty brightening botanical with antioxidant and cell-culture data but no controlled human skin-tone trial found.
lead: Rice bran extract is a cosmetic ingredient derived from the bran layer of rice (Oryza sativa), a by-product of milling. It is used in skincare, especially K-beauty and J-beauty products, for brightening, moisturizing and antioxidant effects .

name: Flutamide topical (melasma)
summary: An oral prostate-cancer antiandrogen studied as a 1% topical for melasma, with a thin evidence base and liver warnings on the oral drug.
lead: Flutamide is a nonsteroidal antiandrogen taken by mouth, used mainly for prostate cancer. It blocks androgen receptors . A 1% topical preparation has been studied as an alternative treatment for melasma, a pigmentation disorder of the face .
